themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase—suggesting a sudden new problem with bike clutter or abandoned Citi Bike infrastructure in Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 6 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.78 indicates statistically significant spike
1100% increase from baseline suggests new or acute condition, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview Citi Bike or NYPD sanitation on whether a single location (e.g., station, transit hub) is accumulating abandoned bikes
Canvass Ocean Parkway and Midwood residential blocks to identify visual hotspots and resident frustration

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints nearly doubled to 17 this week from an 8.1 weekly average, a 109% increase, indicating an emerging environmental and public health problem in the district over the past 7 days.
evidence: 17 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
109% spike occurred within a single week, suggesting concentrated or coordinated activity
reporting_angles: Map the 17 complaints geographically to identify if dumping is concentrated near industrial areas, vacant lots, or transit access points
Interview Sanitation Department on whether they've observed patterns (construction debris, residential waste, hazardous materials) and whether enforcement patrols have increased

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked 878% to 22 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 2.2 weekly average—a sustained elevation over the past 2 weeks—suggesting organized or widespread tagging activity in Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
878% spike indicates acute outbreak rather than seasonal variation
reporting_angles: Investigate whether tagging targets specific property types (residential, commercial, transit infrastructure, schools) or is random
Interview NYPD Graffiti Task Force on whether they've identified crews or connected tags to a single artist or gang

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Peak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 8 three weeks ago—a 2033% spike from a 0.4 weekly average—suggesting a sustained advertising or squatter signage problem that has persisted over the past 3 weeks in the district.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 15.75 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
2033% increase suggests concentrated campaign or failure in enforcement response
reporting_angles: Document the location and content of illegal postings (political, commercial, event promotions, squatter notices) to determine if organized
Check with DOE and MTA on whether postings target schools, bus shelters, or other high-visibility public property

themes_detail.label: Appliance Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Appliance-related complaints (likely broken stoves, refrigerators, and broken landlord-provided units) jumped 182% to 31 last week from an 11.0 weekly average, suggesting housing maintenance failures affecting multiple units over the past 7 days.
evidence: 31 appliance complaints last week vs. 11.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
182% increase suggests either a supply chain disruption (repairs unavailable) or coordinated landlord negligence
reporting_angles: Interview HPD on whether there's a pattern of complaints from specific buildings or landlords, and whether violations have been issued
Contact tenant advocacy groups to assess whether residents are experiencing delays in repair requests and to gather personal impact stories
